title: Dependency free router module for node:http
when: A Node server has a long if and else chain on req.url and needs a small reusable router with path parameters, method matching and 405 answers, without installing packages.
prompt:
Goal: router.mjs that compiles route patterns once, extracts params, answers 404 and 405 correctly and runs async handlers safely.
Steps:
1. Export createRouter() returning { add(method, pattern, handler), use(hook), handle(req, res) }.
2. Compile "/users/:id/posts/:postId" once into a RegExp: replace each :name with (?<name>[^/]+) and anchor with ^ and $.
3. In handle, parse new URL(req.url, "http://internal"), drop one trailing slash except on "/", and run decodeURIComponent on each param inside try (400 on bad escapes).
4. Path matches but method does not: 405 with an Allow header naming the methods of that path; HEAD runs the GET handler and sends no body.
5. Run hooks in order, then await handler({ req, res, params, query: url.searchParams }) inside try and catch, passing errors to one onError(err, req, res).
6. No route at all: 404 JSON.
Quality bar:
- Patterns are compiled at add time, never per request.
- Static routes win over param routes, so /users/me beats /users/:id.
- No global state: tests build fresh routers.
Pitfalls:
- Matching against req.url with the query string still attached.
- Answering 404 where 405 is correct.
- Async handler rejections that crash the process.
Verify:
- [ ] 405 responses carry Allow.
- [ ] Bad percent escapes give 400.
- [ ] A throwing handler reaches onError.
- [ ] A test covers static before param ordering.
Output: router.mjs and test/router.test.mjs.

examples.input: make a tiny router for my node server, no packages
examples.output: createRouter with :params, 405 plus Allow, HEAD support, onError hook, tests
